summary: Flying Cloud Airport is a general aviation reliever airport located in Eden Prairie, a southwestern suburb of Minneapolis, Minnesota. Operated by the Metropolitan Airports Commission (MAC), it serves as a key alternative to Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport for private, corporate, and flight training operations. The airport is one of the busiest general aviation fields in Minnesota and features a single primary runway (10/28) along with multiple FBOs and aviation service providers.
faqs:
Q: Does Flying Cloud Airport have commercial airline service?
A: No, Flying Cloud is a general aviation-only airport with no scheduled commercial flights. It primarily serves private pilots, business jets, and flight training.

Q: Where exactly is the airport located?
A: The airport is in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, roughly 15 miles southwest of downtown Minneapolis, despite bearing the Minneapolis name.

Q: Who operates Flying Cloud Airport?
A: The airport is owned and operated by the Metropolitan Airports Commission (MAC), the same authority that runs Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport.

Q: Is there a control tower at Flying Cloud?
A: Yes, the airport has an air traffic control tower operating during published hours to manage the high volume of general aviation traffic.
transport_tips: Since the airport has no commercial service, ground transportation typically requires a personal vehicle, rideshare, or taxi arranged in advance. The airport is conveniently located near major highways including US-212 and I-494
